S58.01.note: The list comes from the local registry file (~/.agiworkforce/mcp.json) and project MCP files; the code shows no account or workspace-level server list.
steps: Run: agi mcp list
Look for one row per registered server, each with its name, a status word (enabled, disabled or blocked), its transport and its target.
If no servers exist, look for the line that names the registry file.
Compare with Expected: a list of configured MCP servers.
S58.01.where: Type "agi mcp list" in a terminal, or type "/mcp" in the agi chat screen

S58.02.needs: a local executable for a stdio server
S58.02.note: The product starts a stdio server only when a session starts or /mcp restart runs; the add command itself does not launch it.
steps: Run: agi mcp add my-local-server --command node --arg server.js (use any executable on this Mac)
Read the confirmation line that starts with "Registered MCP server".
Run: agi mcp list and check the new row appears with status enabled.
Run: agi mcp get my-local-server and check the transport shows stdio and the target shows the command.
S58.02.where: Type "agi mcp add <name> --command <executable>" in a terminal (in chat, "/mcp add <name> stdio <command>")

labels.text: Header for a remote server as "Name: value", for example an API key. Repeat for each.

S58.03.needs: a remote MCP server URL; a token if the server needs one
steps: Run: agi mcp add my-remote --url https://example.com/mcp (use a real remote MCP URL)
Read the line that starts with "Registered MCP server".
Optional credentials: add --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>" to the same command, then check with agi mcp get my-remote.
Run: agi mcp list and check the row shows the URL with status enabled.
S58.03.where: Type "agi mcp add <name> --url <url>" in a terminal (in chat, "/mcp add <name> <url>")

labels.text: Replace an existing entry with the same name.

S58.04.note: There is no interactive editor screen; editing is done by re-running add with --force (or /mcp reconfigure in chat).
steps: Run: agi mcp get my-remote and read the name, status, transport, target and file lines.
Run: agi mcp add my-remote --url https://new.example.com/mcp --force to replace the entry.
Run: agi mcp get my-remote again and check the target now shows the new URL.
Compare with Expected: the URL, transport and arguments can be viewed and changed.
S58.04.where: Type "agi mcp get <name>" in a terminal to view, then "agi mcp add <name> --url <url> --force" to edit

labels.text: Environment variable for a stdio server as KEY=VALUE, repeat for each.

S58.05.note: The --env flag applies only to stdio servers (it requires --command). Env values are not shown by agi mcp get in the code read; no in-chat env command was found.
steps: Run: agi mcp add my-local-server --command node --arg server.js --env API_REGION=us-east-1
Read the line that starts with "Registered MCP server".
Run: agi mcp get my-local-server and check the file line points to the registry where the entry is stored.
Compare with Expected: the variable is set for the stdio server.
S58.05.where: Type "agi mcp add <name> --command <executable> --env KEY=VALUE" in a terminal

labels.text: Authorize a remote MCP server over OAuth and store the token.
The token is stored in the OS credential store.

S58.06.needs: an outside account (the remote server's sign-in) and a remote server that offers OAuth
S58.06.note: Token-based credentials are entered with --header at add time; the stored OAuth token location is the OS credential store per the confirmation text.
steps: Run: agi mcp login my-remote (for a remote server that offers OAuth)
Complete the sign-in in the browser that opens.
Read the line that starts with "Authorized MCP server" and check it says the token is stored in the OS credential store.
Optional: run agi mcp logout my-remote and read the sign-out result line.
S58.06.where: Type "agi mcp login <name>" in a terminal (for OAuth), or pass --header when adding a remote server

S58.07.needs: a registered server (a remote one needs a reachable URL)
S58.07.note: A disabled server shows only the turn-on hint and no connection test. /mcp test runs the same reconnect as /mcp restart.
steps: Make sure the server is enabled (agi mcp list shows enabled).
Run: agi mcp get my-remote and wait up to 20 seconds.
Read the connection line: it shows a connect error or "did not answer within 20 seconds" on failure, and the tool list on success.
Compare with Expected: the result shows whether the connection succeeded.
S58.07.where: Type "agi mcp get <name>" in a terminal, or "/mcp restart" in the agi chat screen

S58.08.needs: a connected MCP server that offers tools
steps: Connect a server first (agi mcp get <name> or /mcp restart).
In chat, type: /mcp tools
Read the heading "MCP tools:" and check each tool row lists its server name and description.
Optional: type /mcp tools <server-name> and check only that server's tools appear.
S58.08.where: Type "/mcp tools" in the agi chat screen, or "agi mcp get <name>" in a terminal

labels.text: Run a connected server's prompt as /mcp:<server>:<prompt>

S58.10.needs: a connected MCP server that offers prompts
S58.10.note: Prompt commands are registered only when the server offers prompts; the [MCP: prefix text is built in tui_app.rs.
steps: Connect a server that offers prompts (/mcp restart).
Type / in the chat input and look for commands whose description starts with [MCP:<server-name>].
Choose one and run it, then read the reply in chat.
Compare with Expected: the prompt is listed and runs.
S58.10.where: Type "/" in the agi chat screen and find the entries that start with "[MCP:", or type "/mcp:<server>:<prompt>"

S58.11.note: The Capabilities line lists the advertised capability names; resources, prompts and extensions are not shown as separate sections in the code read.
steps: Connect the server first (/mcp restart).
In chat, type: /mcp info <server-name>
Read the Protocol line, the server name and version, and the Capabilities line.
Compare with Expected: protocol, tools, resources, prompts and extensions are visible.
S58.11.where: Type "/mcp info <server>" in the agi chat screen, or "agi mcp get <name>" in a terminal

labels.text: No output from this server yet.

S58.12.note: No call history view was found; only status and recent output lines are shown.
steps: Connect the server first (/mcp restart).
In chat, type: /mcp info <server-name> and read whether it says responding or not responding.
Type: /mcp logs <server-name> and read the Recent output section.
Compare with Expected: health and recent logs are visible; no call history was found in the code.
S58.12.where: Type "/mcp info <server>" for health, or "/mcp logs <server>" for recent logs, in the agi chat screen

labels.text: Turn a registered MCP server off without removing it.

S58.13.note: A running session keeps a disabled server until /mcp restart.
steps: Run: agi mcp disable my-remote and read the Disabled MCP server line.
Run: agi mcp list and check the status is disabled and the row is still there.
Run: agi mcp enable my-remote and check the status returns to enabled.
Compare with Expected: the server is kept while off and can be turned back on.
S58.13.where: Type "agi mcp disable <name>" and "agi mcp enable <name>" in a terminal, or "/mcp disable <name>" and "/mcp enable <name>" in chat

S58.14.needs: a project folder you can write to; a terminal for the first approval
S58.14.note: The approval step and the project-only scope are from code read; the exact on-screen review prompt was not confirmed.
steps: In a project folder, create a .mcp.json file with one server entry (or run agi init, which creates mcp.json).
Start agi from that folder in a terminal and approve the project servers when asked (the code says Run /trust grant in agi).
Type /mcp in the chat screen and check the server appears under the project scope.
Start agi from a different folder and check the server does not appear.
S58.14.where: Put a .mcp.json file in the project folder, then type "/mcp" in agi started from that folder

S58.16.needs: a server on a private network
S58.16.note: Searched apps/cli/src/mcp for private network, relay, tunnel and bridge wording; only a URL check (apps/cli/src/mcp/registry.rs validate_remote_url) and unrelated sandbox text were found, and no private-network connector route was found.
